rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 reproduced the iteration 1 design exactly (score 75.9694, identical per-track metrics), so the baseline is reliable and the s-bend progress of 0.29 is repeatable for this design and seed set. Every lever tested since then lowered the score. kd is the only controller term that has moved s-bend progress: kd 0.1 gave about 0.155, kd 0.15 gave 0.155, and kd 0.2 gave 0.29. That trend is not yet resolved above 0.2, so kd 0.25 is the next untested point, as the Evaluator requested. kp 2.5 (iteration 3) left max_error at 0.062 to 0.065, speed changes (1.2, 1.5) moved progress in opposite directions across tracks without fixing max_error, and sensor spacing or footprint changes cut progress. Max_error has stayed at about 0.061 to 0.065 on every track under every setting, so the off-track failure is not yet addressed by any lever. Change: kd 0.2 to 0.25, everything else unchanged (kp 2.0, ki 0, base_speed 1.4, weights -2..2, sensors at x -0.02..0.02 and y 0.04, sensor_size 0.012, last_direction line loss, same geometry). Expected result: if the s-bend progress trend continues, progress rises above 0.29 and steering_oscillation rises above 0.23, which trades jitter for progress. Hypotheses: (H1) kd 0.25 raises s-bend progress above 0.29 while the oval stays near 0.16. (H2) If s-bend progress falls or oscillation grows past about 0.3 with no gain in progress, kd 0.2 is the optimum and the baseline should be kept for the final evaluation. (H3) max_error stays near 0.06 to 0.065 regardless, so the remaining error is set by bend reach and dynamic lag. Measurements wanted: progress, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, and max_error with its location on the s-bend and slalom.
